title: Ops Scaler: Inference Battle Dash (Draft)
content:
Slide 1 - One-line objective:
Ops Scaler: nine-minute field play to qualify, fix, and hand off inference incidents during pilots (latency/cost/resilience).

Slide 2 - When to use this deck:
- Early pilot (first 2 weeks) where platform engineers are validating latency SLOs and fallbacks.
- Sales + SE on call with customer execs when an incident risk surfaces but you need to keep the pilot running.
- Quick enable for on-call CS/SE to triage and escalate without deep infra deep-dives.

Slide 3 - Core narrative (elevator):
- Problem: Pilots stall when a single integration or model variant spikes cost/latency and SEs lack a short, trusted runbook.
- Promise: 9-minute ops play to stabilize the customer experience, preserve evidence for RCA, and keep the pilot moving towards Reserved capacity or Dedicated trial.
- Outcome: Reduced pilot dropouts, faster handoffs to SRE/Platform, and measurable uptime during demos.

Slide 4 - Quick triage checklist (3 mins):
1) Confirm scope: Is the issue latency, errors, or cost spike? (Check route dashboard + client app logs)
2) Swap to known-stable model variant (pin to lower-latency quantized variant)
3) Toggle prefix cache / KV cache bypass if stale responses suspected
4) Enable temporary rate-limit (workaround) and notify customer of limited degraded mode
Notes: commands/snippets in linked script repo (see linked_artifacts).

Slide 5 - Fallback ladder (how to degrade gracefully):
- Level 0: Transparent mitigation (auto-batching adjustments, increase batching window slightly)
- Level 1: Model variant fallback (e.g., 30% traffic to quantized v1)
- Level 2: Regional failover to alternate region with spare Dedicated pool
- Level 3: Apply cached responses for non-critical routes (embed cache) + notify product owner
Speaker note: each level must include a rollback step and a timestamped audit entry.

Slide 6 - Sample seller scripting (30s):
- Opener: “We’ve put the pilot into a protective mode so your users keep getting responses while we finish the fix. We’ll follow up with the RCA and a remediation timeline.”
- If asked about quality: “We routed a small % to a quantized variant and will measure NPS/QA samples. If unacceptable, we roll back.”

Slide 7 - Metrics to capture during the play (for handoff):
- 1-min/5-min P95 latency pre/post mitigation
- Error-rate delta (502/504s) by route
- Token-cost per request delta (USD estimate)
- User-visible degradation rate (requests served from cache or degraded path)
- Timeline + actions for RCA (who did what, when)

Slide 8 - Quick RCA template (fill in during play):
- Symptom observed:
- First detection time:
- Immediate mitigation applied:
- Who applied mitigation:
- Short-term outcome (metrics snapshot):
- Next owner for full RCA:

Slide 9 - Common objection playbook (what sellers and SEs should say):
- Objection: “Why didn’t this show up in the dashboard?” -> Say: we track rolling distributions; this spike fits a tail-case pattern, we kept a cap on production traffic and triggered fallback. We will add targeted alerting tied to this route.
- Objection: “Will fallback affect model quality?” -> Say: We only route X% to fallback until we validate; quality sampling is included as a required step.

Slide 10 - Demo rehearsal checklist before on-customer call:
- Confirm mock spike scenario works in staging (use test token and traffic generator)
- Verify scripts run in <8 minutes (time the play)
- Ensure Bills/Cost owner notified if token-cost > $Y/hour
- Prepare 1-sentence status update for CSM and customer

Slide 11 - Playbook glue notes (ops/SE handoff):
- Tag the incident with pilot id and route: pilots/{org}/{route} in incident tracker
- Attach the metrics snapshot CSV + the model versions used
- Invite SRE if mitigation required region-level changes (Level 2+)

Slide 12 - To-dos and open questions (work-in-progress):
- TODO: add pre-built shell script to toggle model-variant traffic split (JIRA-OPS-781)
- TODO: map typical pilot routes (embed, chat, rerank) to recommended fallback variant list
- Open: how often should we auto-create a degraded-mode alert for pilots vs. full customers?
- Open: SLA language to propose in pilot contracts for temporary degraded mode? (legal review needed)

Appendix A - Command snippets (quick reference):
- curl toggles for split: curl -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/admin/split -d '{"pilot_id":"P-123","split":{"stable":0.8,"fallback":0.2}}'
- cache flush: rcli cache flush --route pilots/{org}/{route}
- metric export: rcli metrics export --start t-10m --end now --format csv > pilot_snapshot.csv

Appendix B - Notes to self (choppy):
- Need a one-click console button for "enter degraded pilot mode" (ops team ping)
- Consider adding a lightweight SLA clause that covers "protection mode" for pilots to avoid surprise billing
- Shortlist of 3 model variants that are cheapest w/acceptable quality (ask Applied ML for v0.5 list)

References + links: see linked_artifacts above and Confluence page CONFLUENCE-ONRAMP-142 for background pilot definitions.

Last section - Next steps (owner: Maya):
- Iterate script snippets + runbook with Ethan this week (target: 2025-03-05)
- Run 2 staged drills with SE team and record timing
- Convert to compact pocket-card for field sellers (1 pager)

End of draft.

NOTES: informal language allowed; this is a working deck for SE & Ops. Still missing: final visuals, actual curl tokens obfuscated before sharing with customer, legal check on pilot SLA language.
